Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. In my current role at Lukovac Freight Hub, I own the design, ingestion, orchestration and day-to-day operation of a production data platform built with Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka. I would bring that hands-on platform experience to a team building shared, reusable data capabilities for analysts, data scientists and product teams.

Recent work includes building a shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day, with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95, and adding dead-letter and replay tooling to reprocess failed events without data loss. I also migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into tested, documented dbt models, introducing incremental processing and clearer lineage while reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. In 2024, I reduced monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.

My earlier experience at Kovalent Pay is especially relevant to Halden Pay’s payments work. I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR for a transaction reconciliation engine matching bank settlement files against internal ledgers, reducing manual finance-team reconciliation from around three days to four hours per month-end. I have also contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests. Alongside mentoring engineers and running data-platform office hours, these experiences reflect the ownership, collaboration and practical focus on reducing complexity that I would bring to the role.

I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Northgate Technical University, where my thesis was about incremental materialized views. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building and operating data platforms could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses concrete scale and outcome metrics—30 million events per day, sub-two-minute p95 latency, a warehouse build reduction from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes, and Snowflake cost reduction from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month. The Kovalent Pay reconciliation example is particularly relevant to Halden Pay’s payments context. The letter also demonstrates ownership, operational experience, mentoring, and open-source contribution without becoming overly long. Its main content weakness is that it does not explicitly state several relevant terms from the job description, especially data modelling, SQL, cloud data warehousing, and query optimisation. It could also connect the candidate’s experience more directly to Halden Pay’s shared-platform and data-quality responsibilities.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard paragraphs, no tables or graphics, conventional headings are not required for a cover letter, and the job title and company name appear clearly. It includes strong matching keywords such as data platform, Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, Kafka, Python, PySpark, AWS EMR, data quality, and open-source contribution. AI screening probability is strong because the letter contains quantified evidence and role-relevant context rather than a generic motivation statement. However, keyword coverage could be improved by explicitly using supported terms such as SQL, data modelling, cloud data warehouse, production data platform, data quality standards, reusable data capabilities, and query optimisation only if the candidate can substantiate the latter. Do not add Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Docker, or graph modelling because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with the core platform responsibilities: designing, building, and operating a production data platform; operating streaming and batch pipelines; improving reliability and cost; using Airflow and dbt; and contributing to open source. The payments relevance is credible through the transaction reconciliation engine at Kovalent Pay. The letter also supports the company’s Ownership and Pace themes through operational ownership, measurable improvements, replay tooling, and complexity reduction, while mentoring and office hours support the collaborative aspect of Together. The candidate material shows strong evidence of comparable AWS-based cloud experience, but not Google Cloud specifically. Advanced Python and SQL are partly evidenced, although query optimisation on large datasets is not clearly demonstrated. Graph modelling and Portuguese are not evidenced. Data modelling is present in the candidate material but is not stated clearly enough in the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the first paragraph, revise the sentence beginning “I would bring that hands-on platform experience” to include supported job terminology and the shared-platform context. For example: “I would bring that hands-on experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses at scale to a team building shared, reusable data capabilities for analysts, data scientists and product teams.”
2. In the second paragraph, after the sentence about migrating approximately 300 stored procedures, add an explicit data-modelling and SQL reference supported by the candidate’s experience. For example: “This work strengthened SQL-based data modelling, introduced incremental models, and gave analysts clearer lineage.”
3. In the third paragraph, make the comparable-cloud experience more visible by changing “I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR” to “I built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR and worked with AWS-based data services including S3, Glue Data Catalog and Redshift.” This is supported by the candidate’s portfolio and better matches the requirement for comparable cloud experience.
4. In the third paragraph, add one sentence connecting the candidate’s quality experience to the role’s data-quality responsibilities, using only supported information: “I also worked on data quality with Great Expectations, giving me practical experience improving trust in production data.”
5. In the closing paragraph, replace “my experience building and operating data platforms” with “my experience building and operating production data platforms, improving data quality, and simplifying data workflows.” This more directly mirrors the role while remaining supported by the candidate information.
6. Do not add Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Docker, graph modelling, Portuguese, or an unsupported claim about query optimisation. If mentioning SQL optimisation, use only a specific example that the candidate can substantiate; the current source material demonstrates warehouse-cost and build-time optimisation, not clearly query optimisation.

Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. In my current role at Lukovac Freight Hub, I own the design, ingestion, orchestration and day-to-day operation of a production data platform built with Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka. I would bring that hands-on experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses at scale to a team building shared, reusable data capabilities for analysts, data scientists and product teams.

Recent work includes building a shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day, with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95, and adding dead-letter and replay tooling to reprocess failed events without data loss. I also migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into tested, documented dbt models, introducing incremental processing and clearer lineage while reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. This work strengthened SQL-based data modelling, introduced incremental models, and gave analysts clearer lineage. In 2024, I reduced monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.

My earlier experience at Kovalent Pay is especially relevant to Halden Pay’s payments work. I built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR and worked with AWS-based data services including S3, Glue Data Catalog and Redshift for a transaction reconciliation engine matching bank settlement files against internal ledgers, reducing manual finance-team reconciliation from around three days to four hours per month-end. I also worked on data quality with Great Expectations, giving me practical experience improving trust in production data. I have also contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests. Alongside mentoring engineers and running data-platform office hours, these experiences reflect the ownership, collaboration and practical focus on reducing complexity that I would bring to the role.

I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Northgate Technical University, where my thesis was about incremental materialized views. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building and operating production data platforms, improving data quality, and simplifying data workflows could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately tailored to Halden Pay’s Data Platform role. It leads with current platform ownership, gives several quantified achievements, connects the Kovalent Pay experience to payments, and closes with relevant education and motivation. The strongest evidence includes the 30-million-events-per-day pipeline, the dbt migration, Snowflake cost reduction, and reconciliation improvement. The letter is slightly dense in the middle paragraph, but it remains readable and focused. No unsupported claims were detected when cross-referenced against the supplied candidate notes and portfolio.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-relevant terms supported by the candidate’s material, including production data platform, cloud data warehouses, Python, SQL, Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, Kafka, streaming pipeline, incremental processing, data quality, AWS, PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Redshift, Great Expectations, and open-source contributions. Its plain-text structure is parsing-friendly, with no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. AI screening probability is high because the letter contains strong role-specific terminology and multiple quantified outcomes. The main limitation is that it does not explicitly use the ad’s wording around query optimisation on large datasets, although the candidate’s documented warehouse, cost, and build-time optimisation work is relevant.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong. The letter demonstrates designing, building, and operating a production data platform at scale; strong data modelling through dbt and incremental models; comparable cloud experience through AWS, Snowflake, EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, and Redshift; open-source practice through two merged Airflow-provider pull requests; and relevant payments and reconciliation experience. It also reflects Halden Pay’s Ownership, Together, and Pace themes through platform ownership, mentoring, practical problem-solving, and complexity reduction. The candidate material does not show Google Cloud specifically, graph modelling, Portuguese, or direct responsibility for governance rules and access policies; these are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects in the letter. Collaboration with data scientists and product teams is also not directly evidenced in the supplied material.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, after the sentence ending “removal of unused tables,” make the scale and optimisation relevance more explicit without claiming unsupported query-optimisation experience. For example, add: “Together with the dbt migration, this gave me practical experience optimising large-scale Snowflake workloads for both cost and processing time.” This accurately connects the documented Snowflake cost reduction and warehouse-build improvement to the job’s optimisation requirement.
